muted._derivedFrom: Milestone 11 audit. The third step for text that is genuinely meant to be READ but should recede — captions, meta lines, legends, placeholders, breadcrumb separators. It exists because those were all painted in text.tertiary, which fails WCAG AA at normal sizes on every surface (see core.json's gray._500_origin). Reach for this whenever the content is small text; reach for text.tertiary only when it is an icon, a rule, a disabled control, or type at 24px+.

tertiary._derivedFrom: NOT SAFE FOR NORMAL-SIZE TEXT. 3.88:1 / 3.36:1 / 3.09:1 against background.primary / surface.card / surface.cardHover — it clears the 3:1 non-text and large-text floors and nothing more. Correct for icons, decorative rules, disabled content and type at 24px+. For small text that has to be read, use text.muted.

success._derivedFrom: Milestone 7 accessibility review: emerald.500 (the original ref) computes to 4.19:1 against surface.card, failing WCAG AA's 4.5:1 text minimum — a case Design System Bible Ch.3 Section 8 hadn't computed (it only checked background.primary, where emerald.500 passes at 4.85:1). emerald.400 is the same hue/saturation lightened by the same proportional step Ch.3's own crimson.500-to-400 pair already establishes for this exact need.

default._derivedFrom: core.color.white.050 at core.opacity.100 — precomputed since the build pipeline does not perform generic alpha compositing

glassNavFill._derivedFrom: core.color.black.900 at core.opacity.720, paired with core.blur.subtle as backdrop-filter at point of use

glassNavFillReceded._derivedFrom: Ch.20 §5 (Nv-4): recession reduces glass-nav's 72% opacity to "approximately 55%" while remaining above Ch.3 C-3's minimum contrast threshold for any text still visible against it.

glassBackdropFill._derivedFrom: core.color.black.950 at core.opacity.800, paired with core.blur.pronounced as backdrop-filter at point of use

drawerBackdropFill._derivedFrom: Ch.24 §5 (Dw-2): a Drawer's dimmed backdrop is "approximately 40%, no blur" — lighter than Ch.23's Dialog backdrop, reflecting a Drawer's lower interruption level.

buttonBlockSm._derivedFrom: INTERIM — Ch.18 §4 names padding.component-sm/md/lg as a button's padding without splitting inline vs. block; applied literally as padding-inline (matching the token's own name), with these buttonBlock* tokens covering the unaddressed block-padding axis so buttons keep sane proportions rather than becoming square.
